title: Adjoint chain maps on restriction kernels: maps and homotopies
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites with abelian sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor whose precomposition sends abelian sheaves to abelian sheaves, and let $R:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ be $R(G)(W)=G(uW)$, and suppose $L\dashv R$ is an additive adjunction [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $L$ preserving kernels and cokernels. Here an adjunction means natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(LF,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,RG)$; bounded below means the terms are zero in all sufficiently negative degrees. Let $m:V\to T$ and $m':V'\to T'$ be monomorphisms in the two sites, and let $t:T'\to uT$ and $s:V'\to uV$ satisfy $u(m)\circ s=t\circ m'$. For a sheaf cochain complex $I$ on $\mathcal C$ set $A_m(I)=\ker(I(T)\to I(V))$ degreewise and write $D_m(I)$ for its diagram $A_m(I)\to I(T)\to I(V)$, with inclusion and restriction. Use integer-indexed complexes and the derived localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

(1) For complexes $I,J$ on $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ and a chain map $h:LI\to J$, let $b:I\to RJ$ be its degreewise adjoint. The maps $I(T)\xrightarrow{b_T}J(uT)\xrightarrow{J(t)}J(T')$ and $I(V)\xrightarrow{b_V}J(uV)\xrightarrow{J(s)}J(V')$ commute with restriction. They induce a unique map $A_m(I)\to A_{m'}(J)$ compatible with the inclusions, and together give a morphism $D_m(I)\to D_{m'}(J)$.

(2) If $h-h'=d_Jz+z\,d_{LI}$ for degree $-1$ sheaf maps $z$, the degreewise adjoints of $z$, evaluated and restricted along $t,s$, give compatible homotopies on the three components of these diagram maps. In particular the map on kernel complexes is homotopy invariant. If $I,J$ are bounded-below complexes of injective abelian sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions], every derived morphism $a:Q(LI)\to QJ$ has such a representative $h$, unique up to homotopy, and the induced maps on the three cohomology groups depend only on $a$. These cohomology maps are unchanged under the canonical identifications obtained by replacing $I,J$ with other bounded-below injective representatives of the same derived objects.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, pp. 65-67, pair functoriality; agent-formulated chain-level map and homotopy refinement of returned Step 7. Derived representative input: Stacks derived.tex Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective).

proof.text: Let b:I→RJ be the degreewise adjoint of h; it is a chain map because the adjunction bijection is natural in both variables and h is a chain map (the adjoint of d_J∘h^n is R(d_J)∘b^n and that of h^{n+1}∘L(d_I) is b^{n+1}∘d_I). Each b^n is a morphism of sheaves I^n→RJ^n, so for the arrow m:V→T of 𝒞 naturality of b^n gives J^n(u(m))∘b^n_T=b^n_V∘I^n(m), where (RJ^n)(m)=J^n(u(m)). Hence J(m′)∘J(t)∘b_T=J(t∘m′)∘b_T=J(u(m)∘s)∘b_T=J(s)∘J(u(m))∘b_T=J(s)∘b_V∘I(m), using the relation u(m)∘s=t∘m′ and contravariance of J. That is, the composite I(T)→J(uT)→J(T′) followed by restriction to V′ equals restriction I(T)→I(V) followed by I(V)→J(uV)→J(V′). These maps commute with differentials because b is a chain map and the differentials of J are sheaf maps, natural in the object. This is the pair-functoriality asserted in Milne, Section 9, Theorem 9.4, written degreewise.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, pp. 65-67 (naturality of pair maps)

proof.text: The commutative square in Step 1 sends the kernel A_m(I)=ker(I(T)→I(V)) into A_m′(J)=ker(J(T′)→J(V′)). The universal property of a kernel gives a unique map A_m(I)→A_m′(J) whose composite with the kernel inclusion is the T-component map. Together with the T- and V-component maps this is a morphism of the three-term diagrams D_m(I)→D_m′(J); compatibility with both structure arrows is exactly the commutative square already checked. This is a direct degreewise argument in the abelian categories of abelian groups.

Let c:I→RJ be the degreewise adjoint of the degree -1 map z. Applying the same evaluation and restriction composites to h-h′=d_Jz+z d_{LI} and using functoriality of differentials gives b-b′=d_{RJ}c+c d_I, and the corresponding equality after evaluation at T and V′. Restricting this equality to kernels gives a degree -1 homotopy between the two kernel-component maps; the T- and V-components are homotopies as well, and the structure squares commute with them. Hence all three diagram maps are homotopic and induce identical maps on cohomology.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, pp. 65-67, with the chain-level homotopy refinement stated here

proof.text: A bounded-below complex of injective objects is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Therefore the target J is K-injective, and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies morphisms Q(LI)→QJ with homotopy classes of chain maps LI→J. It supplies a representative h for every derived morphism a and says that two such representatives differ by a chain homotopy. Since L is additive and preserves kernels and cokernels, it is exact and the complexes LI remain bounded below, so the stated hypotheses apply.

source.place: Lemma 070I (lemma-K-injective), together with the Mathlib K-injective comparison used by the existing leaf nodes

proof.text: Apply Steps 1--3 to any representative h of a; by Step 3 changing h within its homotopy class does not change any of the three cohomology maps. Composition: for chain maps g:I″→I on 𝒞 and g′:J→J″ on 𝒟, naturality of the adjunction in each variable gives that the adjoint of g′∘h∘L(g) is R(g′)∘b∘g, so its T-component is J″(t)∘g′_{uT}∘b_T∘g_T=g′_{T′}∘J(t)∘b_T∘g_T (naturality of g′ at t), and likewise at V. Hence the diagram map of g′∘h∘L(g) is the composite D_{m′}(g′)∘(diagram map of h)∘D_m(g), where D_m(g), D_{m′}(g′) are the diagram maps of the identity adjunction with t,s identities (Steps 1--2 for u=id). Representatives: if I″ is another bounded-below injective representative and φ:QI″≅QI the given identification, by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] φ is Q(g) for a chain map g:I″→I, unique up to homotopy, and g is a homotopy equivalence with homotopy inverse ḡ. Since L is additive, L(g) is a homotopy equivalence (L carries homotopies d z+z d to homotopies), so Q(Lg) is the induced identification Q(LI″)≅Q(LI) and a″=a∘Q(Lg) is represented by h∘L(g). By the composition identity its diagram map is (map of h)∘D_m(g), and by Step 3 applied to g∘ḡ≃id, ḡ∘g≃id, H(D_m(g)) is an isomorphism with inverse H(D_m(ḡ)), the canonical identification of the three cohomology groups. Similarly for J″ with g′:J→J″ representing the identification, a″=Q(g′)∘a represented by g′∘h, whose diagram map is D_{m′}(g′)∘(map of h). Thus after transport along these canonical isomorphisms the cohomology maps agree, and they depend only on a.
